7.4 — Ladders II: Mounts, Tops & Polish

Your ladder works in the middle — and fails at both ends. Today: the top-of-ladder problem (the hardest 3 tiles in platformer engineering), the mount prompt, and the polish pass that makes climbing feel like an answer to a question the level asked.

Concept Lab ~15 min

The top-of-ladder problem. Climb to the top of yesterday's ladder (7.3) and keep holding W. You rise INTO the floor above (or hover at the seam, depending on your geometry). Every game with ladders has solved this; the three classic answers:

SolutionFeelCost
Stop-at-top: when grounded ABOVE the ladder top, exit climb stateHonest, suddenNeeds a check: raycast down when climbing past the top
Pop-off: climbing W past the top applies a small hopFlows into a jumpPhysics fiddly — can overshoot into enemies
Platform top: a solid tile caps the ladder; you stop under itCheap and commonYou must JUMP the last bit — level design must allow it

Socratic

The starter's levels use the third answer mostly — capped ladders. Why is the CHEAPEST solution often the most honest one? What does the player learn about your game's rules from a capped ladder vs. a magic pop-off?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — implement stop-at-top. In the climb branch, when W is held and your ground raycast (you already own it from 6.2 — extend its reach) finds solid ground at your feet while climbing, exit the climb state cleanly:

// while climbing, if there is floor under my feet at the top:
if (Physics2D.Raycast(transform.position, Vector2.down,
        groundCheckDistance + 0.6f, groundLayer))
{
    isOnLadder = false;
    rb.gravityScale = 2;
    // snap onto the ledge: tiny translate toward it, or leave
    // it to physics — play with both, choose one
}

Step 2 — the mount prompt. The middle of a ladder works by walking into it — but the BOTTOM of a tall ladder often sits above the player's reach. Add a one-liner prompt (same UI family as your HUD thinking): when within range of a ladder's base, show "Press W to climb" text for exactly as long as the condition holds. Cheap version: a trigger zone at the base toggling a world-space TextMesh visible/hidden. The rule: prompts die the instant they are obeyed or no longer relevant.

Step 3 — polish passes (pick two).

  • Animation: add a Climb parameter to the animator; drive it from isOnLadder, and let climbing idle vs. climbing move show different frames
  • Sound: a soft tick per climb-step (your feet know the ladder's rung count — or just a heartbeat)
  • Ladder edges: at the bottom of the climb state, restore a tiny gravity moment so you do not hang in the air when the trigger ends
  • Ladders through platforms: your one-way platform tinker from 7.2 lets a climb pass THROUGH the cap — the two features love each other

Bug Hunt: Endgame of ends

  1. At the top, you exit climb WHILE holding W, grounded on the ledge. But your code above still runs the translate BEFORE the check. What happens on the frame after the exit — one-frame drift INTO the ledge? Fix the order, then explain why one frame of a 60fps game still matters.
  2. The prompt appears when you can reach the ladder BASE, but you jump UP to the trigger from below. Should the prompt appear mid-jump? Why is "prompt when possible" the wrong rule — what IS the right one?
  3. Two ladders back-to-back (a ladder shaft). The exit trigger of ladder 1 fires at the seam... does your enter of ladder 2 fire before the exit? Draw the two messages on a timeline; who wins?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Ladder levels

  1. Design a "chimney": two ladders 3 tiles apart with enemies patrolling the top. What is the player reading during the climb — and why is climbing a PERFECT vulnerability window (you cannot jump away mid-climb)?
  2. Make the ladder the SAFE route and the jump route the fast-but-spikey one. Which do testers choose — record it, this is 9.5 data in the wild.
  3. Commit + push: "7.4a: ladder tops + mount prompt + polish".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain the top-of-ladder problem and implement stop-at-top with a raycast
  • Build a mount prompt that dies when obeyed
  • Drive climb animation from state you already track
  • Reason about order-of-operations on the exit frame
